From: Tomasz (Legal Counsel, Kestrel Payments)
Subject: Contract review timing

Hello, I have been asked to handle the contract from our side. Legal review sits with me and normally takes three weeks for a SaaS agreement of this size; the data processing addendum goes to our privacy officer, Ines, who usually needs a further week. We will work from our standard MSA rather than yours. Once I clear it, the agreement goes to Freya, our CFO, who signs all software contracts above fifty thousand, and then to procurement to raise the order. snippets.body: Rep: Ruaridh, I wanted to get this over the line today. As I said in the proposal, our customers see fifteen percent fuel savings on average and the licence pays for itself in months. I have already put the contract into our e-signature tool, so it is just a case of your legal team clicking through; that normally takes a couple of days at most. From what I understand the decision is made and it is only signature routing left, so if we can get it done by Friday I can hold the discount. I will also line up onboarding for the first week of next month and send the kickoff agenda. Does Friday work? Buyer (Ruaridh, Transport Planning Lead, Vantage Freight): I will need to check.

Rep: How did the evaluation sheet land after last week? Buyer (Ana, Warehouse Systems Lead, Vantage Freight): We wrote it up properly. Five rows, weighted: depot feed as-is at thirty percent, override speed at twenty-five, price at twenty, support at fifteen, and the audit trail row you suggested at ten; Ruaridh and I both signed it off and it went to the steering pack. Buyer 2 (Ruaridh, Transport Planning Lead, Vantage Freight): Agreed, that is the sheet. Rep: What is the cost of the problem today? Buyer 2: Two planners lose three hours every evening rebuilding routes, and we want that under thirty minutes. Rep: How does it show up? Buyer 2: Half-empty trucks leave and the planners take the blame. Rep: Who approves, and when? Buyer: Probably the operations director, sometime this quarter. Rep: Anyone else you are considering? snippets.body: Rep: Post-demo notes, Lumen Retail. Demo went well, Freya was engaged throughout and is clearly our champion. Marta the CFO will be the approver, I would think, given the amount. Criteria as I see them are ease of use and integration with their portal. The pain is the invoice rekeying, probably costing them a couple of days a month per person. Decision likely by the end of the quarter via Marta; security will be a formality, they use the same tooling as our other retail customers, so I expect a month. The only real competitor is the incumbent, who they are unhappy with. My model gives a forty percent reduction in close effort. Next: send pricing and propose a workshop with finance.

Rep: Lotte, is the incident number the one that matters to you? Buyer 2 (Lotte, Operations Director, Halvorsen Marine): It is. We log about forty scheduling incidents a month and I need that under ten before the summer season starts in May; Sinead pulled the baseline from the ticketing system this week and I report that figure to the board monthly. Buyer (Sinead, IT Manager, Halvorsen Marine): Confirmed, forty is the average over six months. Rep: Where do the other options stand? Buyer 2: The incumbent crewing suite cannot run offline on the vessels, rebuilding our own tool means another year of weekend patching, and doing nothing means we cannot crew the extra summer routes, which is not acceptable. Rep: Who signs? Buyer: Lotte, above sixty thousand. Rep: Timing? Buyer 2: Before May, ideally. Rep: And the problem in one line? Buyer: The in-house tool breaks on every rota change and my engineers patch it at weekends.
